Principle 06 of 8

Safety

Do not sell known harms, keep service promises, and allow repair.

Protects

Customers, the public

Why it matters

People trust that what they buy will not hurt them and will work as promised. Concealing a defect turns that trust into risk.

Covers

Service quality, safety, recalls, repair, and refunds (Category 8).

Practices that break it

7.2 Health & Safety Claim Misrepresentation · 10 practices

Safety+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
7.2.1Disease-Cure Claims Without ApprovalMarketing supplements, products, or services as treatments, cures, or preventatives without FDA-equivalent evidence.Supplements, cannabis/CBD, beauty, baby products
7.2.2Structure-Function StretchingExaggerating legitimate structure-function claims to imply disease treatment through implication, imagery, or context.Supplements, beauty
7.2.3Reduced-Risk Without AuthorizationMarketing products as reduced-risk or modified-risk without regulatory authorization.Tobacco/vaping
7.2.4Cessation / Quit Claims Without EvidenceImplying products help users quit (smoking, drinking) without clinical evidence.Tobacco/vaping, supplements
7.2.5Direct-to-Consumer Disease AwarenessRunning ads that medicalize normal conditions to drive demand for branded treatments.Pharma/biotech, healthcare
7.2.6Pet Health Halo ClaimsUnverified therapeutic or developmental claims on pet supplements, baby products, or food.Pet industry, baby/children's products, food
7.2.7Health Halo on Junk FoodHighlighting a single positive attribute ("whole grains," "no artificial flavors") on otherwise nutritionally poor products.Food/beverage manufacturing
7.2.8Anti-Aging Fear MarketingPositioning normal aging as a problem to be solved with fear-based messaging.Beauty, cosmetics
7.2.9Developmental-Milestone ClaimsUnsubstantiated claims that products accelerate cognitive or physical development in children.Baby products, education
7.2.10Lifestyle Health BrandingAssociating addictive products with fitness, wellness, or self-care to recast addiction as health.Tobacco/vaping, alcohol

8.1 Recall Delay & Safety Defect Concealment · 8 practices

Safety+ Honesty
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
8.1.1Recall DelayDelaying recalls of known-defective products to avoid financial impact, even when defects are known to cause harm.Automotive, baby/children's products, firearms, food/beverage manufacturing, pet industry, pharma, home appliances
8.1.2Defect Concealment via SettlementSettling individual defect claims under NDA rather than issuing broader warnings.Automotive, consumer products
8.1.3Crash / Incident Data OpacityCollecting detailed safety data but not sharing it with safety researchers or regulators.Automotive, ride-hailing, airlines
8.1.4Emissions Defeat DevicesUsing software or hardware to circumvent emissions or safety testing.Automotive
8.1.5Sleep-Product MisrepresentationMarketing inclined sleepers, soft bedding, or bumper pads as safe despite contraindication from pediatric guidelines.Baby/children's products
8.1.6Maintenance Deferral for SchedulePostponing required maintenance to preserve on-time performance metrics.Airlines, public transit
8.1.7Safety Defect NDA SettlementSettling individual defect claims under NDAs that prevent broader public warnings.Automotive, healthcare, consumer products
8.1.8Test-Result SuppressionSuppressing internal test results that indicate safety failures (microbiological, chemical, contamination).Food manufacturing, pharma, automotive, beauty

§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

Safety+ Accountability
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in

8.8.5Refund Gatekeeping in SoftwareImposing arbitrary play-time limits or opaque processes that prevent refunds for defective products.Gaming
8.8.6Lost-Package Accountability GapsClaim processes with short windows, burdensome proof, or liability caps that leave consumers uncompensated.Logistics, shipping/freight

11.6 Hazardous Conditions & PPE · 11 practices

Safety+ Responsibility
§PracticeDescriptionSeen in
11.6.1PPE Cost Shifting to WorkersRequiring workers to purchase their own respirators, gloves, or protective clothing.Cleaning, agriculture, pest control, chemical manufacturing
11.6.2Hazardous Condition ExposureFailing to provide protective equipment, shade, ventilation, or safe conditions for high-risk work.Agriculture, cleaning, construction, mining
11.6.3Chemical Exposure Non-DisclosureFailing to inform workers about specific chemicals, exposure levels, or known health risks.Chemical manufacturing, oil/gas, cleaning, pest control
11.6.4Reproductive-Hazard ConcealmentFailing to warn workers of documented reproductive hazards (mutagens, teratogens, endocrine disruptors).Chemical manufacturing
11.6.5Cancer-Cluster Non-InvestigationDeclining to investigate or acknowledge elevated cancer rates among workers when internal data suggests facility-related causation.Chemical manufacturing
11.6.6Heat / Fatigue Risk NeglectAssigning extended outdoor or extreme-temperature shifts without mandated rest or hydration.Staffing/temp, agriculture, waste management
11.6.7Black-Lung / Dust-Exposure ConcealmentSuppressing or manipulating dust exposure data to avoid implementing required controls.Mining
11.6.8Fatigue-Risk NormalizationScheduling that creates chronic fatigue in safety-critical operations without mitigation.Oil/gas, airlines, transit, shipping
11.6.9Pressure to Speed Causing Unsafe DrivingUnrealistic delivery time estimates and late-arrival penalties that incentivize reckless driving.Food delivery, ride-hailing, shipping
11.6.10Production Quotas Compromising SafetyPick-and-pack or daily-job quotas that force workers to skip breaks or compromise safety.Logistics, warehousing, pest control, shipping
11.6.11Housekeeper WorkloadExcessive room counts per shift with piece-rate pay that incentivizes skipping safety protocols.Hospitality
